title: Example 18-5: Isolated Punctuation Is Emphasized

illustrates.quote: When isolated punctuation is emphasized with something other than italics, bold, underlining, or script, insert a transcriber’s note after the punctuation mark or applicable word to identify the print emphasis.

blocks.text: Full sentence (back-translated from the given braille): "I didn't think so, but that's it." — with an embedded transcriber’s note reading "apostrophe is red" inserted immediately after "that's" and before "it." (the apostrophe in "that's" is printed in red). Not modeled: F-186, no mechanism exists to insert a @.<...@.> note mid-sentence, only as a standalone block.

print.notes: Verified by back-translating the given braille as a whole (the two runs’ own separate guesses for the note text and sentence disagreed on where the note sits relative to "it."; back-translation removes the ambiguity: the note falls between "that's" and "it.").
print.printFeatures: The phrase "but that's it." is italicized; the apostrophe in "that's" is red.

braille.notes: Re-extracted from source (lines 14429-14430, margin 9); matches both runs byte-for-byte.

resolution: Braille already agreed and re-extraction confirms it exactly. print.blocks left as a single 'other' limitation (F-186, already the section’s own documented finding, its own Example 18-5 evidence) rather than an ordinary paragraph, since the note is fused into the middle of the sentence, not separable from it; building a paragraph without it would misrepresent what this example actually demonstrates.
